A1.justification: Both complete, readable 18-page PDFs describe XHugWBC. The main text, figures, tables, equations, and Appendices A–B support comparison, including matching renumbered appendix tables.

before.justification: V1 reports original simulation benchmarks, fine-tuning experiments, architecture ablations, and physical-robot demonstrations in Section 4 and Appendix B.

after.justification: V2 retains those original results and adds quantitative simulation-versus-hardware tracking measurements in Section 4.5 and Table 2.

M1.justification: V2 explicitly describes an upper-body intervention training switch in Section 3.3. V1 already includes I(t) in observations and rewards and reports teleoperation, but does not explain this switch, leaving its status as a new procedure versus newly documented behavior unresolved. The main-text masked-first attention architecture remains unchanged.

E1.justification: The simulated embodiments, seven physical robot configurations, and locomotion/loco-manipulation tasks are retained. The new fixed-speed comparison evaluates existing robots and locomotion coverage; it adds a protocol rather than a distinct task or environment.

E2.justification: HugWBC specialists, MetaMorph, MorAL, and Naive Random remain in their corresponding comparisons. V2 newly states that Naive Random uses XHugWBC's Transformer architecture, without reporting a change to that baseline or its results.

E3.justification: Section 4.5 adds a focused sim-to-real protocol: command 0.6 m/s for 10 seconds, estimate average velocity from distance divided by time in both domains, and calculate tracking errors and normalized gaps. Existing simulation evaluation settings in Appendix B.1 are retained.

E4.justification: New RQ5, Section 4.5, and Table 2 provide a targeted analysis of transfer discrepancies across seven existing physical platforms. The architecture ablation and latent-representation analysis in Figures 6 and 4 remain unchanged.

E5.justification: V2 specifies five repetitions and reports their means for the added sim-to-real test. This does not establish increased replication of earlier experiments. Existing plus/minus summaries remain unchanged, and the new table supplies no variability estimates or confidence intervals.

E6.justification: Table 2 adds paired simulation/hardware tracking errors and reports degradation on every platform, with normalized gaps of 27.45%–107.93%. For example, Dobot Atom has errors of 0.063 and 0.131 m/s. These are new protocol-specific results, not improvements over v1; existing benchmark values and curves are retained.

T1.justification: Appendix A.3 revises the formal attention specification: Equation (28) assigns masking to MAB rather than SAB, and Equation (29) changes the operator composition to SAB ∘ SAB ∘ ... ∘ MAB. This is a localized mathematical correction; the physics-consistency lemmas, Proposition 3.5, and Appendix A.1 proof remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions and claims about cross-humanoid generalization, twelve simulated embodiments, seven physical robots, approximately 85% of specialist return, and fine-tuning gains up to 10%. The added transfer-gap evidence does not redefine these core claims.

C2.justification: Section 3.1 now qualifies mass-based gain and torque scaling as a heuristic approximation. Section 4.5 adds interpretations attributing transfer discrepancies to robot scale and platform-specific actuation, reducers, and joint clearances, while acknowledging unavailable external ground truth. The conclusion's existing command-interface limitation is retained.

D1.justification: V2 documents the upper-body intervention behavior and explicitly identifies Naive Random's matching Transformer architecture. It also names Unitree G1 and H1-2 in the retained manipulation experiment. Randomization ranges, reward weights, deployment infrastructure, and resource-access information otherwise remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Appendix A.3 adds Liu et al. (2025b), Skill latent space based multigait learning for a legged robot, as a state-estimator reference. The related-work discussion and novelty positioning otherwise remain substantively unchanged.

P1.justification: V2 adds the intervention explanation and RQ5, and reorganizes the former real-world subsection into separate sim-to-real and loco-manipulation subsections. Other changes are localized wording, grammar, and terminology corrections rather than extensive rewriting.

P2.justification: V2 adds Table 2, corrects the encoder/estimator block order and labeling in Figure 2, and reduces Figure 7 from nine frames to six. Existing plots and appendix illustrations are retained, with local layout shifts and appendix-table renumbering.

improvement.justification: V2 improves empirical transparency by supplementing v1's physical-robot success claims and demonstrations with controlled, repeated tracking measurements that expose transfer errors. Clearer baseline and control documentation also helps reproducibility. The gain is limited by the single-speed test, mean-only reporting, and remaining inconsistencies in Appendix A.3's explanations of masked and unmasked attention.
